newsitem.title: JAPAN: Coastguard suspects error caused Tokyo oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Coastguard suspects error caused Tokyo oil spill.

text.p: Japan's coastguard said on Thursday it suspects human error led a supertanker to hit a reef an spill oil in Tokyo Bay.
The Panamanian-registered supertanker Diamond Grace struck a reef off Yokohama on Wednesday morning, rupturing at least two of its tanks.
"The pilot said the tanker did not suffer any mechanical or engine failure," coastguard operations coordinator Saburo Sunaga told a news conference.

The pilot, Seiji Ushio, 57, who was on board, had also told coastguards that the tanker had not been trying to avoid a collision with another ship. "So we suspect the accident was caused by some form of human error," said Sunaga.
But he said maritime authorities had not finished questioning the captain, Hidenori Tsunematsu, 55, and it was too early to pinpoint the exact cause of the accident.
Yokohama maritime authorities were questioning the pilot and the captain to see whether there were any violations of rules that led to the accident, a coastguard spokesman said.
Authorities had said that the tanker leaked an estimated 13,400 tonnes or 100,000 barrels of crude oil but on Thursday officials revised the figure down to 1,315 tonnes.
The ship, a very large crude carrier (VLCC), was loaded with 257,000 tonnes of crude oil from the United Arab Emirates and heading for a refinery in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo.

At its shallowest point, the Nakanose undersea reef is only 12 metres (37 feet) below the surface. But it is marked by navigational aids, including not only buoys, but a sophisticated radar network and computer-aided locating services.
The tanker reached port in Kawasaki under its own power on Wednesday evening, and coastguard officials and the captain plan to inspect it later on Thursday.
